preamble: APOL1-Associated Kidney Disease  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  KDIGO 2021 CKD Guidelines / AASK Trial / APOL1 Long-term Kidney Transplantation Outcomes (APOLLO) Study  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Are two APOL1 high-risk alleles (G1/G1, G1/G2, or G2/G2) confirmed? (Prerequisite: required for all prognostic scoring in this agent)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — APOL1 high-risk genotype confirmed; foundational risk marker; penetrance ~20–30% lifetime

questions.question: Is there an active inflammatory or viral trigger known to amplify APOL1 nephrotoxicity? (HIV viremia, active SLE, interferon therapy, SARS-CoV-2 infection)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — second-hit trigger present and active; APOL1 channel opening accelerated; rapid CKD progression expected

questions.question: Is there established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or metabolic syndrome coexisting with APOL1 nephropathy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high cardiovascular-renal risk burden confirmed; synergistic CKD accelerators beyond APOL1 alone

questions.question: Is proteinuria ≥1 g/day (urine PCR ≥1.0 mg/mg) at current assessment?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant proteinuria confirmed; reflects active podocyte injury; strongest modifiable progression driver

questions.question: Has proteinuria worsened ≥50% from baseline over ≥6 months despite RAS blockade?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — rising proteinuria on therapy; treatment-resistant disease activity; consider APOL1-specific trial enrollment

questions.question: Is eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 4) at current assessment?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severely reduced eGFR; ESRD within 3–5 years at median APOL1 progression rate; transplant planning indicated

questions.question: Is annualized eGFR decline >5 mL/min/1.73m²/year confirmed on ≥3 serial measurements over ≥12 months?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — rapid progression confirmed; APOL1 nephropathy median decline 5–7 mL/min/year vs. 1–2 for typical CKD

questions.question: Is collapsing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis confirmed on kidney biopsy? (strongest APOL1-associated histologic pattern)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — collapsing FSGS confirmed; 50–70% ESRD risk within 3 years; APOL1-mediated podocyte collapse

questions.question: Is there moderate-to-severe tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis (>25% of cortex) on biopsy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significant chronic injury confirmed; irreversible nephron loss; limits renoprotective treatment response

questions.question: Is BP persistently ≥140/90 mmHg despite ≥3 antihypertensive agents including ACE inhibitor or ARB (uncontrolled hypertension)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — refractory hypertension confirmed; APOL1 nephropathy has disproportionate hypertension burden and is ACE/ARB-resistant in severe cases
